title: The Resurrection of the Dead
sourceBasis: World English Bible — 66-book Old and New Testament Scripture text already installed in Iron Sharpener
definition: The resurrection of the dead is God’s future raising of all people, the righteous and the wicked, for final life or judgment. Death is not the end, and every person will stand before God.
summary: The resurrection of the dead is God’s future raising of all people, the righteous and the wicked, for final life or judgment. Death is not the end, and every person will stand before God.
christFocus: Jesus Christ is the risen Lord and the firstfruits of resurrection. Because He lives, the dead will be raised, His people will receive resurrection life, and His victory over death will be openly displayed.

studySections.heading: Doctrine in Summary
studySections.content:
Scripture teaches a future resurrection of the dead. Human life does not dissolve into nothingness, and death does not remove accountability before God.

The resurrection includes both the righteous and the wicked. Those who belong to Christ are raised to life, while those outside Christ face judgment.

This doctrine is grounded in the resurrection of Jesus. Christ is not merely an example of hope; He is the firstfruits, guaranteeing that death will not have final dominion.

The resurrection of the dead gives seriousness and hope to life now. Bodies matter, choices matter, faith matters, and God’s promises extend beyond the grave.

studySections.heading: Why This Matters
studySections.content:
Many people live as though death ends everything, while others imagine vague spiritual survival detached from bodily resurrection. Scripture gives a clearer hope and warning.

This doctrine strengthens believers facing death, grief, disability, sickness, and decay. God will raise the dead, and Christ’s victory will be seen in full.

studySections.heading: Discipleship and Application
studySections.content: Live in light of resurrection. Do not treat your body, choices, suffering, or faith as meaningless. Look to Christ, comfort grieving believers with resurrection hope, and warn the lost with humility that death does not end accountability.
